speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia associated with Down Syndrome.

The physical exam findings of epicanthus, upward slanting eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease are classic for Down Syndrome, which is strongly associated with duodenal atresia. The bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance in a newborn with these features and a "double bubble" X-ray sign (implied by the clinical picture of distal obstruction despite normal US for malrotation) confirm the diagnosis.
